answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A reputation system then releases the deposit only after useful work is verified, while proven fraud forfeits it. Splitting one operator into a hundred identities does not create a hundred free chances: each must tie up capital, and each exposed identity risks losing its stake. The jetty, grove, and terrace can be separate task markets, but the same costly bond follows an agent across them. This raises the attacker’s cost without pretending that deposits alone prevent Sybils.
